blocks.x: Foundation models are converging on capability; the durable advantage sits in retrieval, permissions and freshness.
The retrieval layer is the moat, not the model. Every enterprise answer should cite its source paragraph — provenance is the feature that survives audit.
Permission-aware retrieval turns your existing entitlements into AI guardrails for free.
Freshness SLAs on corpora are the difference between trusted assistants and abandoned demos.

Where it breaks in practice: retrieval appended after the model choice, permissions mapped after launch, freshness treated as an ops afterthought — each producing the same symptom: answers nobody defends when the audit arrives.

The strongest counter-case, stated fairly: the retrieval-first thesis can excuse weak models. It should not: retrieval multiplies whatever the model does, so evaluation stays the arbiter in both directions.
How we put it to work

In delivery, this thesis becomes a specific discipline: we build the assistants, classifiers and retrieval systems that carry the decision, then hold them to an eval set your reviewers recognize as their own. Every program in the Applied AI & GenAI domain carries the same obligations — a signed baseline, named gate criteria, and evidence generated by running the system rather than preparing for a meeting.
Start with the diagnostic, not the contract: this position baselined against your estate in two weeks, and a scoped proposal only if the delta justifies it.
